card.architecture: MiniMax-H3 ref2va (Qwen3-VL 32B, int8 ConvRot) — REFERENCE-TO-VIDEO with native audio
card.summary: Generate a clip whose SUBJECT is taken from your reference image(s), with NATIVE stereo audio — voice, sound effects and music generated together with the motion. The current image is the primary subject reference; add more via the ＋ ref picker. The references condition identity/appearance (they are NOT the first frame). Output is an mp4 with a baked-in audio track.
use_cases: reference→video: place a referenced subject into a new clip with synchronized sound
multi-reference identity (subject from several angles / a few characters)
generate motion + audio around a subject without pinning a first frame
card.pick_when: You want a NEW clip featuring the subject from your reference image(s) — not to animate the current picture as its literal first frame (use MiniMax-H3 image→video for that).

prompt.guidance: Refer to each reference by its tag — the open image is <Picture 1>, picker images continue <Picture 2>…, video clips are <Video 1>…, audio clips <Audio 1>… (1-based per type). Say which reference drives which element (identity, setting, motion, voice), then add an 'Audio:' line.
prompt.example: Insert the woman from <Picture 1> into the scene of <Video 1>: use the setting, lighting and actions from <Video 1>, and the woman's appearance from <Picture 1>. Audio: distant city traffic, footsteps on wet pavement, a moody synth line.
prompt.overview: The reference image(s) define WHO/WHAT appears — the model knows them only by their tags: <Picture i> for images (the open image is <Picture 1>), <Video k> for clips, <Audio j> for audio. State explicitly which tag drives identity, which drives setting/motion/camera, and which drives voice; then add an 'Audio:' line so H3 generates the soundtrack (ambience, effects, dialogue, score) jointly with the motion.
prompt.instructions: Reference every attachment by its exact tag (<Picture 1>, <Video 1>, <Audio 1> — 1-based per type; no other tag names work) and assign each a role: e.g. 'the person from <Picture 1>' for identity, 'the setting and motion from <Video 1>'. Describe the action with concrete verbs (speed + direction), specify a camera move, and add atmosphere. Then add an 'Audio:' section describing ambience, timed sound effects, any dialogue, and score. Don't re-describe the referenced subject's static appearance (the references define it). Quote spoken lines. Timeline cues like [0s-2s] help place motion and audio beats.
do: Refer to references by their tags: <Picture 1>… / <Video 1>… / <Audio 1>…
Assign each tag a role: identity, setting, motion, camera, or voice
Describe the scene/setting the subject is placed into
Lead the subject's action with concrete verbs (speed + direction)
Specify a camera move (slow push-in, dolly out, pan, orbit, static)
Add an explicit 'Audio:' line: ambience, timed effects, dialogue, score
Quote spoken lines; use [0s-2s] cues to time beats
dont: Don't invent tag names — it's <Picture 1>, not <Image 1>/<Photo 1>; an unknown tag grounds to nothing
Don't re-describe the referenced subject's static appearance (the references define it)
Don't rely on negative prompts — this is a distilled model
Don't forget the audio: leaving it out wastes H3's main capability
examples: The woman from <Picture 1> walks slowly toward the camera across a sunlit plaza, glancing to her side. Steady dolly-back keeping her centered, shallow depth of field, warm afternoon light. Audio: soft crowd murmur, distant fountain, a gentle acoustic guitar motif.

Insert the woman from <Picture 1> into the scene of <Video 1>: keep the setting, lighting, camera and actions of <Video 1>, replacing its subject with the woman from <Picture 1>. Audio: match the ambience of <Video 1>.

speed.measured_note: large video model with a 32B text encoder; reference tokens ride every sampling step. Not yet benchmarked on this box.

ui_help.note: Generate a clip WITH sound featuring the subject from your reference image(s). Describe the scene, motion and audio.

edit_use_cases: reference-to-video: generate a clip featuring the referenced subject, with native audio

reference.hint: The current image is <Picture 1>; picker refs follow as <Picture 2>…, <Video 1>…, <Audio 1>… Refer to them by those exact tags in the prompt and say which drives identity, setting/motion, and voice.
